correctness.rationale: The exact peripheral normalization follows from the scalar recurrence \(1-s_{t+1}=2s_t(1-s_t)\). The two-season product is explicitly computed, its characteristic polynomial and factored discriminant follow by direct expansion, and its square is positive for every \(0<\alpha<1\). At the unique discriminant zero, Cayley–Hamilton on the sum-zero plane plus a certified nonzero first coordinate of \(N(e_1-u)\) proves a genuine index-two nilpotent part. Binomial expansion gives the claimed identity for every iterate; strict stochastic primitivity and the scalar closed form give convergence. The standalone checker ran symbolic and 220 rational test cases, not used to infer infinite statements.

value.rationale: Two different peripheral transpositions first fail to commute in a three-coordinate peripheral sector, making four total species the smallest natural example in this family. This canonical alternating two-season inheritance scheme exhibits an exactly solvable switch from complex to real damped modes at \(\alpha=2\sqrt3-3\), including polynomial-exponential convergence generated by the defective return map; each normalized one-season exchange kernel individually remains reversible and diagonalizable. The resulting structural relaxation mechanism is not merely a routine tabulated statistic or arbitrary fixed-parameter evaluation.
